questions.prompt: The prospect says “We’re on Glofox.” What’s your first move?

options.text: Acknowledge something real, tie it to where Momence is stronger, then ask about their experience

questions.reveal: Acknowledge first so they don’t dig in, then show the edge.

questions.prompt: Why never open with “their support is bad”?

options.text: Several competitors out-rate Momence on support, and a prepared prospect will check

questions.reveal: You’ll lose the room the moment they pull up the numbers.

questions.prompt: What is a landmine question?

options.text: A question they answer from their own experience that surfaces the cost

questions.reveal: They find the problem. You don’t have to say it.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an attack, not a landmine?

options.text: “What did your price move to at renewal?”
“Their software is buggy and everyone’s leaving.”

questions.reveal: A claim makes them defend. A question makes them think.

questions.prompt: On an SDR call, where should the competitor conversation end?

options.text: On a reason for the meeting

questions.reveal: You’re selling the meeting, not the switch.

questions.prompt: “Is Momence better than MindBody?” Best response?

options.text: Validate, acknowledge their strength and tie it to ours, reframe on cost, then ask about them
Offer to send a comparison PDF

questions.reveal: That’s VARS.

questions.prompt: What is MindBody’s marketplace fee?

options.text: 20% of the purchase, capped at $30, on new clients from the MindBody app

questions.reveal: From MindBody’s own documentation. It sits on top of subscription and processing fees.

questions.prompt: “MindBody’s app brings us new clients.” Best response?

options.text: “That channel is real. Do you know what share of new signups come through it, and what that fee adds up to?”

questions.reveal: Acknowledge the channel, then let them do the math on a fee Momence doesn’t charge.

questions.prompt: Which MindBody strength should you acknowledge before showing the edge?
questions.reveal: Don’t fight it head-on. Ask how many reports they actually pull.

questions.prompt: “WellnessLiving has great reviews. 4.4 on Capterra.” Best response?

options.text: “They do, and day to day people like it. Worth asking how they’d handle a billing dispute before you sign.”

questions.reveal: Both are true: good day-to-day reviews, and a billing pattern on the BBB.

questions.prompt: Which is the best WellnessLiving landmine?

options.text: “If you cancelled tomorrow, how confident are you the charges would actually stop?”

questions.reveal: It surfaces the documented billing pattern without a claim.

questions.prompt: WellnessLiving advertises processing “starting at 2.59%.” What does that tell you?

options.text: It’s a floor, so ask for their actual blended rate
It’s the rate they actually pay

questions.reveal: “Starting at” isn’t what lands on the statement.

questions.prompt: What does Glofox’s own enterprise proposal quote?

options.text: 2.5% per card transaction, free texts, $1 per e-agreement
Free texting on every plan and 1% per card transaction
1.5% per card transaction, $0.05 per text, no e-agreement fee
3.80% per card transaction, $0.10 per text, $3 per e-agreement

questions.reveal: First-party and citable.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest Glofox landmine?

options.text: “What did your price move to at your last renewal, and how much notice did you get?”

questions.reveal: Renewal increases are the verified pattern. Their support rates well.

questions.prompt: “Glofox is built for franchises, and we plan to scale.” Best response?

options.text: Acknowledge their franchise depth, then ask what scaling costs on their per-location structure

questions.reveal: Acknowledge the strength, then reframe on cost.

questions.prompt: What does Arketa’s own pricing page say about transaction fees?
questions.reveal: Close to 6% all in once Stripe is included.

questions.prompt: Which is the best Arketa landmine?

options.text: “When you pull a revenue report, does it reconcile against Stripe?”

questions.reveal: Reporting accuracy is a theme in their own customers’ reviews.

questions.prompt: “We love Arketa’s video.” Best response?

options.text: “Video’s a real strength, and we do live and on-demand too. Worth weighing against the 3% on every transaction.”

questions.reveal: Acknowledge, show we match it, then reframe.

questions.prompt: Which is the best Walla landmine?

options.text: “Besides Walla, what other tools are you paying for: email, SMS, reviews, forms?”

questions.reveal: Consolidation is where Momence wins against Walla.

questions.prompt: “Walla is easier to use.” Best response?

options.text: “They’ve done a great job on simplicity, and we’re easy too. Do you want software for today, or something that grows with you?”

questions.reveal: Acknowledge simplicity, then show where Momence goes further.

questions.prompt: What do Walla customers complain about most?

options.text: Features still being built and limited automation

questions.reveal: Their reviews are strong. The gap is growth, not quality.

questions.prompt: What is the VARS order?
questions.reveal: For “what makes you different?”

questions.prompt: What does the Acknowledge step do?

options.text: Names the competitor’s strength so you can tie it to ours

questions.reveal: Acknowledge, then tie it to where we’re better.

questions.prompt: On an SDR call, how does the Specify step end?

options.text: By making it about their numbers and tying that to the meeting

questions.reveal: “That’s exactly what the AE can walk through with your numbers.”

questions.prompt: Internal notes say Arketa quoted one studio a monthly price. How do you use that?

options.text: Quote it as Arketa’s monthly price for every studio
Say “studios we’ve talked to were quoted around…” or skip it
Round it up a little so the gap with Momence looks bigger
Say it’s the price listed on Arketa’s own pricing page

questions.reveal: One studio’s quote isn’t their published price. State it as fact, and one wrong number costs you the call.

questions.prompt: Where should a competitor fee you cite come from?

options.text: The competitor’s own pricing page, documentation or proposal

questions.reveal: First-party sources are defensible.

questions.prompt: The card says a WellnessLiving feature is unconfirmed, and the prospect asks about it. What do you do?

options.text: Ask how they handle it today, without making a claim

questions.reveal: Ask, don’t assert.

questions.prompt: Why compete on cost structure and contract terms, not general quality?

options.text: Those points are verified and specific, while general quality ratings often favor the competitor

questions.reveal: Fight where the facts are on your side.

questions.prompt: The prospect is on Glofox and renews in 14 months. Best move?

options.text: Push hard for a meeting now
Acknowledge, plant one landmine, get the renewal date and log it

questions.reveal: More than 6 months left, so no meeting yet. Plant the question; it matters at renewal.

questions.prompt: “What does Momence cost compared to MindBody?” Best response?

options.text: Say it depends on their setup, the AE walks through it with their numbers, then ask a question back

questions.reveal: Pricing stays with the AE.
